newsitem.title: USA: Mild weather a relief for North Dakota farmers.
newsitem.headline: Mild weather a relief for North Dakota farmers.

text.p: Mild February weather was a welcome relief to farmers and ranchers, the state agricultural statistics service said Monday in its monthly crop report.
"Moderate weather has lessened adverse weather on livestock. However, ranchers are experiencing calving difficulties with reports of weak cows, light calves and stillborns," the report said.
Cattle conditions were rated three percent very poor, 13 poor, 37 fair, 44 good and three excellent, compared to three percent very poor, 15 poor, 34 fair, 46 good and two excellent on February 16.
Cattle and calf death loss was assessed at 62 percent above normal, compared to 29 percent two weeks ago.
Ranchers in the southwest and south central districts have suffered the highest livestock losses.
Current supplies of hay and forage were rated 41 percent very short to short, compared to 40 percent at that level two weeks ago.
The state average snow depth Sunday was 14.6 inches, versus 16.8 inches two weeks ago and 7.3 inches a year ago.
The report said farmers have been busy transporting grain before posted road restrictions take effect.
